Filesystem isolation for run_candidate_gate() is still partial: the candidate runs in a throwaway cwd with a stripped environment, but there is no chroot or mount-namespace, so it can read whatever the runner's normal file permissions allow. Closing that gap needs a container or mount-namespace sandbox and is flagged as an infra-owned follow-up in the code comment, not fixed by this round.

The network-namespace wrapper (unshare -r -n) was verified on this development container, not on the organisation's actual self-hosted VPS runner named in gates.yml; if unprivileged user namespaces are disabled there (kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0), run_candidate_gate() will fail closed as designed, but that fail-closed path itself was only exercised by monkeypatching NETWORK_ISOLATION_AVAILABLE in a test, not by disabling user namespaces on a real host

The no-userns simulation for this round's namespace-degrade fix shadowed the 'unshare' binary on PATH with a stub that always exits 1, which reproduces what _probe_network_isolation() observes when the kernel rejects the unshare(2) call — it does not cover the separate 'unshare binary entirely absent' branch of that probe (shutil.which returning None), though that branch's code path is unchanged by this round and was already covered by the existing test_network_isolation_probe_is_a_clean_bool test plus manual reading, not by a dedicated absent-binary simulation

The quoted-text-stripping fix for MISSING_TARGET_RE only strips simple single/double-quoted substrings (a regex, not a real shell tokenizer); a needle passed unquoted, or through nested/escaped quoting a real shell would still parse as one token, could still be misread as error text — this covers the common `grep "pattern" file` / `grep 'pattern' file` shapes named in the Greptile finding, not every possible shell quoting form

_load_candidate_check_receipt() (item 1's in-process fallback) imports the candidate module directly rather than running it as a sandboxed subprocess — a materially smaller trust footprint than handing it a CLI invocation with attacker-controlled argv (the only function exercised, check(), is pure: no file/network/subprocess I/O), but module import does still run the candidate's top-level statements in-process. This is a documented, deliberate trade-off to close the 'required job passes untested' gap on hosts without a network namespace, not a claim that it is as strongly isolated as run_candidate_gate()'s unshare(2) sandbox — that sandboxed path remains the primary, preferred execution route whenever a namespace is available.

COMPOUND_EXISTENCE_GATE_RE's 'no captured output' rule only recognises `test -f/-e X && ...` and `[ -f/-e X ] && ...` lead-ins (matching EXISTENCE_ONLY_RE's own alternation); a content search chained after a `stat`/`ls` existence probe, or chained with `;` instead of `&&`, is not covered by this round's fix and would need a follow-up if that shape turns out to matter in practice

ABSENCE_CLAIM_RE is a fixed word list (exists/absent/removed/deleted/gone/not present/no longer exists/no longer present); a differently-worded absence claim that doesn't use one of those words would still fall through to the existing existence-only rejection — this was scoped to the exact wording pattern Greptile's finding used, not exhaustively enumerated against every way a human might phrase 'this path is gone'
